L A Y E R 1 · F O U N D A T I O N
AI Data Center
Why power density changes everything
Traditional DC
< 1 MW, single block
AI Data Center
+3 MW
+3 MW
+3 MW
+ ...
3 MW is the traditional UPS/breaker building block. AI facilities scale by adding 
more of it as GPU rack demand grows — 3, 6, 9 MW and beyond, not one fixed 
size.
That modular, ever-growing power demand means: heavier electrical load to 
manage, more heat to remove, and greater risk if the grid drops. That is exactly the 
gap our four product lines close.
UPS + Battery
Reliable backup power for 
heavier, more critical loads
Precision Air 
Conditioning (PAC)
Removes the extra heat that 
high-density racks generate
Generator Sets
Continuity when the grid fails 
— the stakes are higher now
We sell the power and cooling backbone that scales with the facility, block by block.
4

L A Y E R 2 · C O M P U T E
Servers
With power and cooling in place, the next layer is the hardware that actually runs AI workloads.
AI Server
GPU + NPU + CPU
Traditional Server
CPU only
We sell both — matched to what each workload actually needs.
A global chip & memory shortage
NVIDIA leads GPUs; Huawei leads AI accelerators (Ascend NPUs); Samsung leads 
memory — all in constrained supply. We sell the servers built around them, so this 
scarcity still shapes what we can deliver.

L A Y E R 3 · I N T E L L I G E N C E
Large Language Models
Hardware needs a brain. This is where AI compute becomes AI capability.
Closed-Source
Claude · Gemini · OpenAI · Doubao
Each is tied to one cloud: AWS–Claude, GCP–
Gemini, Azure–OpenAI. Great for API use, but not 
available for private deployment.
Open-Source
Qwen · DeepSeek · GLM · Kimi
Not locked to one cloud — can be self-hosted for 
free on infrastructure the client controls. Note: 
several open-source families (e.g. Qwen, 
DeepSeek) also ship a closed-source hosted version 
of the same model.
The key insight
Because closed-source models are bound to a single cloud, 
they can’t be privately deployed. So when a client needs 
on-premise or private deployment, what we actually sell is 
open-source model deployment and integration — not the 
model itself.
Three ways to buy tokens for closed-source models
Open-source is free to self-host — these channels are for paid, closed-source access.
